subject: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form

Kim / Ben,

Looping you in — NovoHealth legal/procurement sent the attached order form redlines (see OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx). Procurement wants clarity on two things before they issue a PO:

- Whether we can accept an invoice "stub" (partial invoice) at signing for their internal accruals, and what documentation we need to support that (activation/commencement date vs. invoice date).
- Confirmation of minimum commit phasing and how we invoice mid-quarter proration + any tax treatment (they asked specifically about VAT/GST residency evidence).

High-level ask: can Legal/Finance confirm our position on invoice stubs and a short checklist we can send back to their procurement team (PO trigger, stub allowed Y/N, required attachments, and net terms impact)?

I've attached our earlier Invoice_Stub_Policy_v1.pdf for reference. If we can finalize a one-paragraph policy and a 3-point checklist today, I'll share it with NovoHealth and keep momentum on the deal.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment(s): OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx (docx), Invoice_Stub_Policy_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-01-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form

Thanks Marcus — reviewed the redlines quickly. Key legal items:

1) Invoice stub: we can allow a single "stub" at signing provided the invoice clearly states it's a pro forma / interim invoice and the final invoice follows once service commences. We need:
   - language in the order form that the stub is for customer internal accounting only and is not an acceptance of services;
   - a supporting commencement statement (signed by customer) or system activation record to validate start date.

2) Net terms: we can accept Net30 on the stub but final invoicing should preserve the agreed net terms tied to the final invoice date. Suggest adding an explicit clause: "Payments on pro forma invoices are applied against amounts due on final invoices; final invoice date determines net term countdown."

3) Tax / VAT: Ask customer for a tax residency certificate (or country-specific VAT registration) for reverse-charge. If they cannot provide, we default to gross-up. Finance to confirm tolerance for evidence types.

I'll draft a short checklist and a redline snippet for the order form. Ben — any commercial concerns on min-commit proration?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal (Commercial) | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): none

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-10T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form

Adding commercial context from Sales ops:

- Minimum commit phasing: we should accept the customer's proposed 3-tranche ramp (25/35/40) but call out an invoice schedule that maps to those tranches. For the stub, we can invoice the first tranche pro forma (25%) at signing.
- Proration: mid-quarter usage beyond committed amounts will be billed in arrears on the final invoice for the quarter — don't mix with stub.
- Net terms / Credits: if stub is paid, that payment reduces the outstanding balance; credits for early termination should reference final invoice accounting.

Recommended action: Marcus, reply to procurement with a one-page checklist (Legal + Sales bullets) and request their PO template + a tax residency document. If they push back on gross-up we can propose a limited 90-day evidence window.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@novohealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novohealth.com, purchasing@novohealth.com
Date: 2027-01-11T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form

Marcus — thanks for the quick response. A couple clarifying points from our side:

- We can provide a PO as soon as we receive the stub invoice and a brief checklist confirming the stub is for accrual. Our finance team requires the stub to include: order number, "pro forma" label, and expected final invoice date.
- Tax evidence: we will attach NovoHealth VAT registration (we are registered in the EU but have a US entity). If you require a specific certificate, please list acceptable docs — VAT reg number + company registration is easiest for us.
- Net terms: Our procurement prefers Net45 on final invoices; can Redwood accept Net45 for this account? If not, we can discuss partial upfront on stub.

Attaching: NovoHealth_tax_evidence.xlsx (contains VAT reg and entity mapping).

Best,
Lina Torres
Head of Procurement | NovoHealth
Attachment(s): NovoHealth_tax_evidence.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@novohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@novohealth.com
Date: 2027-01-12T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Invoice stub policy & minimum-commit / tax checklist for Order Form

Lina — appreciate the turnaround. Summary and next steps below (combining Legal + Sales):

1) Stub policy (we can accept):
   - Redwood will issue a single pro forma invoice for the first tranche (25%) at signing, clearly labeled "Pro Forma — For customer accruals".
   - Customer to include order number on stub. Final invoice issued upon service commencement and will reflect true usage and remaining tranches.

2) Checklist / required evidence from NovoHealth (please provide):
   - VAT registration number or equivalent tax residency documentation (we received the spreadsheet; Kimberly will confirm sufficiency).
   - Signed commencement acknowledgement (one-liner) or activation event timestamp from your team once services go live.
   - PO referencing Redwood order form and indicating stub payment acceptance.

3) Net terms: Redwood prefers Net30 by standard, but for NovoHealth we can agree Net45 on final invoices for this procurement, provided stub payment follows agreed remittance instructions and reduces the outstanding balance accordingly. Please confirm PO will reference Net45 on final invoice.

4) Commercial mechanics:
   - Proration for mid-quarter usage billed on final invoice in arrears.
   - Termination credits calculated on final invoiced amounts (not stub).

Action items:
- Lina: confirm PO will reflect Net45 and upload the signed PO + VAT docs to the DocuSign link (or send via procurement email).
- Kimberly: will confirm tax evidence acceptability and provide the redline snippet for the OrderForm_v3 that references pro forma language.
- Ben: I'll follow up with SRE/Onboarding to confirm activation event format to include in the checklist.

If everyone is aligned I can send a one-page joint checklist (Legal + Sales) to procurement today.

Thanks all,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): Invoice_Stub_Policy_v1.pdf (pdf)
